title: Stalkwise bijectivity of the affine symmetric algebra comparison
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], $W$ an affine open, and $x\in\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_X(W)$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points]. Let $\alpha_W$ be the explicit tilde comparison of [def-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-affine-comparison-map]. Then the induced map on underlying abelian stalks $(\alpha_W)_x:(\widetilde{\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X(W)}F(W)})_x\to(S|_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_X(W)})_x$ is bijective. Here $S$ is the ring sheafification of the sectionwise symmetric algebra [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-sheaf-construction], and stalk maps are colimits of the underlying abelian presheaf maps, as in [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0C6F; Constructions, Lemma 01LN; Schemes, Lemma 01I8

proof.text: Obtain the affine-basis transformation delta. Extend it to gamma:P→T on all opens via TopCat.Sheaf.restrictHomEquivHom. The extension has the prescribed components on the basis. Equality of its composite with alpha and the restricted unit follows from TopCat.Sheaf.hom_ext on the affine basis.

source.place: Lemma 01I8; extension of morphisms from a basis

proof.text: Basiswise injectivity of gamma gives injectivity of gamma_x by stalkFunctor_map_injective_of_isBasis. For surjectivity, exists_mem_germ_eq_of_isBasis represents any target stalk element by a section on an affine V. Lift this section using the surjective component delta_V and take its germ; stalkFunctor_map_germ_apply proves it maps to the desired element.

The restricted ring unit theta_x is bijective. Functor.map_comp turns gamma;alpha=theta into the corresponding stalk factorization. For injectivity of alpha_x, lift two source elements along gamma_x and apply injectivity of the composite. For surjectivity, lift any target element along the composite. This proves the original unchanged statement.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 01I8: affine-basis section reduction, extension by sheaf morphism uniqueness, and stalk bijection cancellation
